svg.title: The lifecycle of a generic TLD domain, and the rules for transfers
svg.desc: A timeline from left to right. Registered: the domain is registered for one to ten years and renews if auto-renew and payment work; you can renew any time, and the registrant email must be monitored. The registrar sends renewal notices about one month and about one week before the expiry date. Expired: after the expiry date the registrar interrupts DNS, usually showing a parking page, while the registrant can still renew at the normal price. Redemption: after deletion the registry holds the name for a 30-day redemption grace period with DNS off and transfers blocked; only the old registrant can restore it, usually for a fee. Pending delete is a short final stage, after which the name is released and anyone can register it. Below, moving to another registrar: unlock the domain and get the authorization code; transfers are blocked for 60 days after registration, a previous transfer, or a change of registrant; move DNS hosting first if the old registrar hosts it, and remove DS records first if DNSSEC is on.

g.text: A generic TLD domain from registration to release
notices about 1 month and 1 week before
Moving the registration to another registrar
1. Unlock the domain (clear clientTransferProhibited) and get the authorization (EPP) code.
2. Expect a block for 60 days after registration, a previous transfer, or a change of registrant.
3. Move DNS hosting first if the old registrar hosts it; remove DS records first if DNSSEC is on.
Auto-renew, a monitored contact email, and expiry alerts keep you out of the red zone.
